steps.name: QC, normalize counts, flag low-library sample
steps.question: Given the 12000x13 Salmon gene-count matrix and the 12-sample (6 anti-PD-1 vs 6 isotype control) metadata table, what is the normalized (CPM/TMM) expression matrix to feed into deconvolution, and how should sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) be handled?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata are loaded and sample IDs are matched/reconciled between the two files (13 count columns vs 12 metadata rows reconciled, extra column identified e.g. gene ID column)
Library size per sample is reported; sample_01 is explicitly flagged as an outlier with its fold-deviation from the median quantified
A TMM- or median-of-ratios-normalized log-CPM matrix is produced and saved for downstream steps
A decision is recorded on whether sample_01 is retained (with a documented caveat) or excluded, plus a sensitivity flag for downstream steps to run both ways if retained

steps.name: mMCPcounter murine immune/stromal deconvolution
steps.question: Using the mMCPcounter method (16 flow-cytometry-validated murine immune and stromal cell populations, self-contained marker set, no external reference file needed), what is the per-sample abundance score for each cell population across all 12 tumor samples, and how do treated vs control samples differ?
acceptance_criteria: mMCPcounter runs successfully on the normalized mouse gene-symbol matrix from T1S1 and returns a cell-type x sample score matrix covering all 16 populations for all 12 samples
Output table includes sample_01 with its score reported alongside the QC flag from T1S1
Per-cell-type treated-vs-control comparison (anti-PD-1 vs isotype control, unpaired, n=6/6) is run using a nonparametric test (Wilcoxon rank-sum) with BH-adjusted p-values across the 16 populations
Results reported both including and excluding sample_01 to show sensitivity to the low-library-size sample

steps.name: Orthogonal PanglaoDB marker-based ssGSEA cross-check
steps.question: As an independent cross-check of the mMCPcounter estimates, what per-sample enrichment scores do mouse-filtered PanglaoDB immune/stromal cell-type marker sets yield via ssGSEA on the same normalized expression matrix, and do they agree in direction with mMCPcounter for the anti-PD-1 vs control contrast?
acceptance_criteria: PanglaoDB marker table is filtered to the mouse ('Mm') species column and converted into per-cell-type gene sets covering major immune/stromal lineages (T cell, NK, B cell, macrophage/monocyte, DC, neutrophil, fibroblast, endothelial) matched where possible to mMCPcounter's populations
ssGSEA (via GSVA) produces a cell-type x sample enrichment score matrix for all 12 samples using the same normalized matrix as T2S1
Treated vs control comparison per cell type uses Wilcoxon rank-sum with BH correction, reported alongside T2S1's results for the matched cell types to assess concordance
Any cell type where ssGSEA and mMCPcounter disagree in direction of the treatment effect is explicitly flagged as inconsistent rather than reconciled by narrative

steps.name: Compositional summary and treatment-effect statistics
steps.question: Integrating the mMCPcounter and PanglaoDB-ssGSEA composition estimates across all 12 samples, what is the overall immune/stromal landscape of each sample, and does composition differ significantly between the 6 anti-PD-1 and 6 isotype-control tumors, either cell-type-by-cell-type or as a whole compositional profile?
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample stacked-composition visualization and a cell-type x sample heatmap are produced for both estimator outputs

A multivariate compositional test (PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis or Euclidean distance of the scaled composition matrix, treated vs control) is run in addition to the per-cell-type univariate tests from T2S1/T2S2
A PCA of the composition matrix is produced with samples colored by condition and sample_01 marked distinctly

Final summary table lists, per cell type: mMCPcounter effect direction/significance, ssGSEA effect direction/significance, and whether they agree, with explicit statement that n=6/6 unpaired is modestly powered and that sample_01's low library size is a documented caveat on its individual estimates
No claim of a significant treatment effect is made for a cell type unless it is significant after BH correction in at least the primary (mMCPcounter) estimator

plan.title: Mouse TME immune/stromal composition, anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 samples, mouse gene symbols) subcutaneous tumor dataset comparing 6 anti-PD-1-treated vs 6 isotype-control mice, unpaired, single batch. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which is a real QC concern for count-based deconvolution and differential testing alike. There is no reference single-cell atlas, LM22-style human signature matrix, or mouse-specific deconvolution package matrix staged directly as a reference file, but the sandbox carries several validated bulk-deconvolution tools that ship their own reference marker sets internally: mMCPcounter (16 mouse immune/stromal populations, validated by flow cytometry per Petitprez et al. 2020, Genome Medicine) and MCPcounter/ConsensusTME/quantiseqr/EPIC (human-oriented, requiring ortholog mapping and weaker for mouse). Because mMCPcounter is purpose-built and flow-validated for murine tumor tissue and needs no external reference file, it is the primary method. A PanglaoDB marker-based ssGSEA/UCell scoring pass (using the staged PanglaoDB mouse markers) is added as an orthogonal, marker-set-based cross-check that does not depend on the mMCPcounter internal model, since a second, independent estimation approach is standard practice for composition claims that will inform a treatment-effect conclusion. The plan proceeds: (1) load/QC counts and metadata, normalize (CPM/TMM), flag sample_01 explicitly rather than silently dropping it, and run mMCPcounter to get per-sample cell-type abundance scores for all 12 samples; (2) run an independent marker-signature scoring pass (ssGSEA via GSVA, using PanglaoDB mouse immune/stromal markers) as an orthogonal validation of composition estimates; (3) statistically compare treated vs control per cell type (Wilcoxon rank-sum given n=6/6, with BH correction across cell types), report effect sizes and a sensitivity check with/without sample_01; (4) produce a compositional summary (stacked bars, heatmap, PCA/PERMANOVA on the composition matrix) integrating both estimators to characterize overall immune/stromal landscape shift under anti-PD-1.
